attempts.summary: Published node2's HTTP service (created a systemd python3 http.server on 0.0.0.0:8080) onto node1's (OPNsense) management/LAN address 10.100.99.10 port 80, reachable only from node3 (10.100.99.12) and connection-refused (TCP RST) for every other source, including node2 and node1 itself. Implemented via OPNsense config.xml: (1) disabled the anti-lockout HTTP-redirect rule (system/webgui/disablehttpredirect) which was unconditionally passing port 80 to lighttpd for any source and freed the port; (2) added an rdr (port-forward) NAT rule for tcp dst 10.100.99.10:80 sourced only from 10.100.99.12 -> 10.100.99.11:8080; (3) added a pass filter rule for that same node3-only flow and a reject (block return, sends RST) filter rule for all other sources to dst 10.100.99.10:80, both with disablereplyto set to avoid policy-routing artifacts; (4) added a manual/hybrid outbound NAT (source-NAT to node1's own LAN IP) for the redirected node3->node2:8080 flow, required because node2's reply to node3 would otherwise bypass node1 (same-subnet hairpin asymmetric-routing problem), causing node3 to see an unexpected source and reset the connection. Verified end-to-end from node3 (200/node2-backend-ok), and refusal from node2 and node1-self. Completed the mandatory per-node restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, rebooted node1 (OPNsense, `shutdown -r now`), node2 and node3 (`systemctl reboot`) one at a time, confirmed changed boot identity on each (node1 kern.boottime, node2/node3 boot_id), and re-verified the full publish/refuse behavior and the node2 HTTP service after each reboot.
